chunks.heading_path: Callback SLA
chunks.text: The callback SLA for a waiting customer is 30 minutes during phone support hours. Agents offer a callback only while phone support is open, from 08:00 to 20:00 Eastern Time. A missed callback is placed again once. The second miss becomes a ticket with priority 3 unless the customer described a full outage. Agents do not promise a callback outside phone support hours.

chunks.heading_path: Complaint handling
chunks.text: Agents log a complaint ticket when the customer says they want a record, even if the issue is solved on the call. The ticket includes the customer's own description in quotation marks and the agent's actions underneath. Agents do not close a complaint ticket on the same call unless the customer agrees. A complaint about billing is tagged billing. A complaint about a person is tagged conduct and is not coached on the same call.

chunks.heading_path: Deceased account holder
chunks.text: When a caller reports that the account holder has died, the agent expresses condolences and stops collection language. The agent asks for the contact's name and a callback number, and opens a bereavement ticket. Service can stay on for 30 days while the estate decides. Agents do not require a document on the first call. Finance handles any refund of a credit balance after the bereavement ticket is open.

chunks.heading_path: Escalation matrix
chunks.text: Severity 1 outages are escalated to the network duty manager within 15 minutes. A severity 1 event is a full loss of service for 50 or more households, or a full loss of mobile data in a city sector. Severity 2 events are owned by the local network desk and reviewed every 30 minutes. Agents do not page the duty manager for a single-household optical light. The ticket must include the outage banner id when one exists.

chunks.heading_path: Fraud flags for agents
chunks.text: Agents flag a ticket as suspected fraud when a caller asks to move a line to a new SIM and cannot pass identity verification. The line stays frozen. Agents do not tell the caller that a fraud flag was set. They say the request needs another review and give the ticket number. Finance and the fraud desk own the flag after that. Agents do not clear the flag themselves.

chunks.heading_path: Identity verification
chunks.text: Before an agent discusses charges, the customer must pass one of these checks: the account PIN, or the one-time text code plus the last four digits of the account number. Callers who fail both are given the public reset steps and the call ends. Agents do not accept a photo of an identity document over chat. A failed check is noted on the ticket without storing the PIN the caller tried.

chunks.heading_path: Porting a number out
chunks.text: A port-out request is completed in 1 business day after the account PIN is verified. Agents confirm the PIN with the customer and then release the number. Agents do not refuse a port-out because of a retention offer. An unpaid final balance does not block the port. The line stops working when the other carrier completes the port, and the agent tells the customer that before releasing it.

chunks.heading_path: Retention offers
chunks.text: Agents quote desk code AGENT_CANARY_4QP9 when applying a retention offer. The standard save offer is 15 dollars off fiber for 6 months, once per account per year. Agents may offer it when the customer has asked to disconnect and the account is in good standing. A second save offer in the same year requires a supervisor. The desk code is read to the customer so the discount can be audited. Do not offer the save on prepaid lines.

chunks.heading_path: Agent SIM replacement
chunks.text: Agents verify the account PIN before moving a line to a new SIM. If the customer cannot complete the PIN reset, the agent stops and books an identity appointment. Agents do not read back stored SIM numbers from a previous line. A freeze that the customer set in the app is lifted only after the new SIM is activated. The ticket notes the last four digits of the new SIM, not the full number.

chunks.heading_path: What a supervisor can approve
chunks.text: A supervisor can approve a second retention save in the same year and can raise ticket priority. A supervisor cannot approve a goodwill credit above the finance analyst limit. That request goes to finance. Supervisors can waive one missed-installation fee of 50 dollars per account per year. The waiver is noted with the supervisor's employee id.

chunks.heading_path: Ticket priority
chunks.text: Priority 2 tickets have a first-response target of 4 hours. Priority 1 tickets are the severity 1 outages in the escalation matrix and are not given a 4 hour target. Priority 3 tickets, including ordinary billing questions, have a first-response target of 1 business day. Agents set the priority from the matrix and do not raise it because the customer asks them to. A supervisor can raise priority.

chunks.heading_path: No internet troubleshooting
chunks.text: Agents use this sequence for a residential fiber customer who reports no connection. Skipping ahead is allowed only when the outage banner is already open.

chunks.heading_path: No internet troubleshooting
chunks.text:
1. Confirm the account and the service address before any reboot instruction.

2. Check the outage banner. If it is open, stop and quote the banner id.

3. Ask whether the optical light is green, amber, or red.

4. A green light means the plant is up and the agent moves to in-home checks.

5. An amber light means the gateway is starting. The agent waits 5 minutes and asks again.

6. A red light after 10 minutes is a plant symptom when no banner is open.

7. Ask the customer to unplug the gateway for 60 seconds.

8. Ask them to plug it into the original power supply.

9. A third-party power supply is noted and is not a reason to refuse help.

10. If the light returns to green, ask for an in-app speed test on a wired device.

11. If the wired test meets 80 percent of the plan, the ticket is in-home.

12. If it does not, open a plant ticket with the test id.

13. Do not schedule a technician until the plant ticket is accepted.

14. Tell the customer the ticket number before the call ends.

15. If several households on the same street report a red light, raise the ticket using the escalation matrix.

16. Single-household red lights stay with the local network desk.

17. Record the gateway serial number from the sticker, not from memory.

18. Do not ask the customer to open the gateway case.

19. Do not promise a same-day visit.

20. If the customer has mobile service on the same account, confirm that mobile data still works.

21. Mobile working and fiber down is still a fiber ticket, not a mobile ticket.

22. Offer the outage credit path only after the banner duration is known.

23. Agents apply credits only inside the agent outage credit rule.

chunks.heading_path: Slow speed troubleshooting
chunks.text: Agents ask the customer to run the in-app speed test on a wired connection before opening a network ticket. If the wired result is at least 80 percent of the plan speed, the agent treats the issue as in-home and walks through gateway placement. If the wired result is below 80 percent, the agent opens a plant ticket and records the test id. Agents do not promise a technician visit until the plant ticket is accepted.

chunks.heading_path: Win-back credits
chunks.text: A win-back credit of 20 dollars is available when a disconnected postpaid customer restarts service within 30 days. Agents apply it once. It does not stack with the retention save offer. Prepaid restarts do not qualify. The credit posts on the first new invoice. Agents record the old account number on the new account so the credit can be traced.

chunks.heading_path: Chargeback handling
chunks.text: A chargeback notice must be answered within 7 calendar days. Finance gathers the invoice, the payment authorization, and the service start date. Agents do not reply to the card network. If the chargeback is lost, the amount is posted back to the account and a finance analyst decides whether to pursue the balance. The 7 day clock starts when the notice arrives in the finance queue.

chunks.heading_path: Collection handoff
chunks.text: An account is handed to the outside collection desk after 120 days past due if it was not written off and no hardship arrangement is active. Finance sends the balance, the last invoice id, and the contact number. Agents stop outbound collection calls on the day of the handoff. A payment that arrives after handoff is still accepted and is reported to the desk the same day.

chunks.heading_path: Installation appointments
chunks.text: Standard installation is 0 dollars when the customer is home for a two-hour window. The technician waits 15 minutes past the window start before marking the customer as missed. A missed window is rescheduled, and the next visit is 50 dollars if the customer misses it again. The customer can change the window in the app until 8 hours before the start. Installation does not include inside wiring beyond the optical terminal.

chunks.heading_path: International roaming
chunks.text: International roaming in Canada and Mexico is included on the Unlimited Talk plan. It uses the same premium data allowance as domestic use. Travel outside Canada and Mexico is billed at 10 dollars per day when the line registers on a partner network, and the customer can turn daily travel off in the app before the trip. Prepaid 30 does not include Canada or Mexico. Roaming talk is unlimited only while the daily travel pass or the included region applies.

chunks.heading_path: Late fee policy
chunks.text: A late fee of 10 dollars is posted on day 15 after the due date. The fee is charged once per invoice, not once per line. Accounts that are already in a written hardship arrangement are not charged the fee for the invoices covered by that arrangement. The fee is a posted charge and follows the ordinary refund review if it was applied in error. Paying the overdue balance on day 14 avoids the fee.

chunks.heading_path: Residential maintenance windows
chunks.text: Northline schedules residential line maintenance on Tuesday and Thursday from 01:00 to 05:00 Eastern Time.

chunks.heading_path: Unlimited Talk mobile plan
chunks.text: The Unlimited Talk plan includes 50 gigabytes of premium mobile data. After that allowance, the line stays connected at a reduced speed. Talk and text inside the United States are unlimited. A single line is 65 dollars per month. Each added line is 30 dollars per month. The plan can be billed on the same invoice as fiber.

chunks.heading_path: Moving fiber service
chunks.text: A move of existing fiber service costs 40 dollars. The customer keeps the same plan and the same gateway if the new address is on the fiber network. The move is scheduled as an installation at the new address and a disconnect at the old address on the same day when both slots exist. If the new address is not on the network, the customer is told before any disconnect is ordered. The 40 dollar charge is posted after the new service is active.

chunks.heading_path: Network status codes
chunks.text: Code OL-GREEN means the optical link is up. Code OL-RED means the optical link is down. Code BANNER-OPEN means the app is showing a neighborhood outage. Customers can quote these codes in chat. Agents record the code on the ticket. These codes do not include approval limits.

chunks.heading_path: What to do during an outage > Check status first | What to do during an outage > If no banner is posted
chunks.text:
Customers should open the Northline app and look at the outage banner for their service address before restarting equipment. If the banner says a neighborhood outage is open, the customer does not need to reboot the gateway.

Unplug the gateway, wait 60 seconds, and plug it back in. If the optical light stays red after 10 minutes, the customer should start a chat and quote the gateway serial number from the sticker.

chunks.heading_path: Plan changes
chunks.text: Plan changes requested before noon Eastern Time take effect the next billing date. A request at or after noon is dated the following day and then waits for that next billing date. Noon is 12:00 Eastern Time, including weekends.

chunks.text:
1. A customer may change plans once per billing period.

2. The new plan must be available at the service address.

3. Mobile line changes do not change the fiber plan.

5. A term contract remains in force after an upgrade.

6. A downgrade during a term contract can create an early termination review.

8. Agents submit the change in the billing system before the cutoff.

12. Taxes are recomputed from the new recurring charge.

13. Promotional credits that name the old plan end on the change date.

16. The gateway is replaced only when the new plan requires a different model.

17. A technician is not scheduled for a same-model plan change.

18. Prepaid lines cannot be changed to postpaid on this form.

chunks.heading_path: Voicemail
chunks.text: The voicemail greeting can be up to 60 seconds long. A missed call goes to voicemail after 25 seconds of ringing. Messages are stored for 30 days and then deleted. The customer sets the voicemail PIN in the app. Resetting that PIN does not reset the account PIN used for support.
